title: Triage thresholds and heuristics — review toolkit (scratch)
content:
Purpose: quick personal playbook for triaging PRs and follow-ups. Wanted something I can scan in 60s during async review windows. Mostly heuristics and cutoff rules I keep forgetting.

Top-level mental model:
- Is this change on the hot path (latency / token loop) or not? If yes -> stricter: unit tests + perf benchmark or hold. If no -> fuzzy checks ok.
- Does the diff touch serialization, persistence, or migration paths? Migration = high cost -> push for more eyeballs.
- Is the change size > ~200 LOC or touches >3 subsystems? If yes -> break up or insist on design doc.

Quick triage checklist (fast pass, 60s):
- Does PR have a clear description of intent? (yes/no)
- Linked issue or design note? (Y/N)
- Summary of testing steps present? smoke/perf/regression?
- Files changed: hot-path? (tokenizer/model|serving|kv-cache|rpc)
- Any binary additions / vendored dependencies?
- CI green? any flaky jobs?
- Author's self-checklist? (e.g., run e2e locally, added unit for edgecases)

Red flags to escalate immediately:
- Changes to KV cache eviction or cache key format -> tag SRE + 2 reviewers, require rollout plan.
- Silent opt-in toggles for behavior (feature flags that default-on) -> insist default-off and a canary rollout.
- Schema changes (DB, telemetry) without migration/rollback notes.
- Changes to tokenization or compilation kernel selection logic -> request perf microbench and correctness tests on short+long sequences.

Heuristic cutoff numbers (my personal thresholds):
- If edits span > 6 files and include one of {serving-runtime, platform-engineering, observability} -> request a short design note.
- If latency-sensitive path and expected RPS bump > 10% -> require perf bench before merge.
- If change touches infra scripts (deploy, infra as code) -> ask infra owner and defer merge until green staging deploy.

Suggested reviewer asks (phrasing templates I use):
- "Can you add a quick note on rollback steps if this regresses in prod?"
- "Why this approach vs small adaptor layer? I'm concerned about coupling to X."
- "Could you add a targeted unit test for the edge-case {X} you mentioned?"
- "Please include a perf snapshot for 512-token and 2048-token sequences (latency and p99)."

Small refactor acceptance guidelines (when to accept without heavy review):
- Pure mechanical renames / comment cleanups limited to a single file -> single reviewer ok.
- Small refactors (<100 LOC) that only touch implementation details, with tests passing and no behavior change -> 1 reviewer + author signoff.
- Any refactor that simplifies an algorithm on hot path -> require benchmark demonstrating no regression.

Follow-up TODO categories (how I log followups in PR comments):
- Followup: add integration test for fallback routing
- Followup: add tracing span around new cache interaction
- Followup: reconcile telemetry naming with metrics team
- Followup: add canary flag and gradual rollout config

Unresolved questions / personal doubts (things to check next time):
- Am I being too conservative with the 6-file rule? sometimes a cross-cutting change is small. Maybe prefer asking the author for a 1-paragraph summary instead.
- How to make perf requests low friction for PR authors — a lightweight harness template would help.

Examples of comments I tend to leave (copyable snippets):
- "Nice cleanup. One nit: rename `handle` -> `handle_async` to indicate it's returning a future."
- "Could you add a test for the case when header 'X' is missing? Edge-case found in prod once."
- "Given this touches the token loop, can you run `bench/token-loop --seq 512 --runs 100` and paste p50/p95/p99?"

Mini protocol for post-merge incidents:
1) If merged and symptoms appear, add `revert` label immediately and notify owner.
2) If revert possible without data loss, do an immediate revert and hotfix.
3) If revert risky, revert trafﬁc via canary config and run targeted diag.

Personal housekeeping (how I keep this doc usable):
- Keep it short. Delete items I haven't used in 3 months.
- Move stable phrasing to Confluence (linked above) and keep this as ephemeral quicknotes.

Notes to self:
- Add a tiny perf harness template under serving-runtime/tools/bench that runs on CI when PR label `perf-check` added. Low effort + big win.
- Propose a 'triage champion' rotation for peak hours to reduce review fatigue.

Scratch ideas for automation (quick wins):
- Bot that flags PRs touching KV cache keys and auto-tags SRE + perf.
- Lint rule that warns on imports of internal 'hotpath' modules from unrelated packages.
- Template for lightweight perf request that runs on a single small GPU in CI and returns p50/p95/p99.

End state: want a 60-second checklist I can run in my head and a 5-minute follow-up plan for medium-risk PRs. This doc is the ephemeral crib-sheet.

-- Sasha

(rough, fragmentary — intended for my own use; move to Confluence if it stabilizes)
